'''''Davallia canariensis''''', the '''hare's-foot fern''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[fern]] in the family Davalliaceae. It is [[endemic]] to [[Macaronesia]] and the [[Iberian Peninsula]]. It grows well in a sunny atmosphere and amongst rocks.

==Description==
''Davallia canariensis'' is a spreading, [[deciduous]] fern with thick, scaly [[rhizomes]] and broad, finely-divided [[fronds]], it grows up to {{convert|50|cm|in|abbr=on}} tall and {{convert|100|cm|in|abbr=on}} broad.<ref name=rhs>{{cite web|title=Davallia canariensis |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/5359/i-Davallia-canariensis-i/Details |publisher=www.rhs.org.uk (RHS)| access-date=17 December 2016}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Davallia canariensis'' is found on the western [[Mediterranean Basin]], from [[Cape Verde]], the [[Canary Islands]] and [[Madeira]] to [[Morocco]] and the western [[Iberian Peninsula]] (western [[Portugal]] and northwest and southwest [[Spain]]). It grows on tree trunks and branches, mossy siliceous rocks in cool and humid places with oceanic influences, from sea-level to {{convert|600|m|ft|abbr=on}} in altitude.<ref name="iberica">{{cite web |title=D. canariensis |url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/01_024_01_Davallia.pdf |publisher=[[Flora Iberica]] |access-date=17 March 2021}}</ref><ref name=rhs/> The Latin [[binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''canariensis'' means "from the [[Canary Islands]]".<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book |last=Harrison |first=Lorraine |title=RHS Latin for Gardeners |year=2012 |publisher=Mitchell Beazley |location=United Kingdom |isbn=978-1-84533-731-5 }}</ref>

As it is only [[hardiness (plants)|hardy]] down to {{convert|5|C|F|abbr=on}}, in [[temperate climate]]s it must be grown under glass as a houseplant. However, it may be placed outside in a sheltered spot during the summer months. It has an [[Award of Garden Merit]] from the Royal Horticultural Society.<ref name=rhs/><ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 29 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 6 February 2018}}</ref>
